title: The Bank of the Invisible: Lucknow, Abu Dhabi, and the Seventy-Eight Countries
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Lucknow, and the Border That Moves

stops.name: Lucknow, the birth in the city of the Nawabs
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia gives the full date
stops.campa: He is born on the fourteenth of May in Lucknow, into an Urdu-speaking middle-class household in the old capital of Awadh. The city keeps a courtly grammar long after the court itself is gone: indirection, and the sentence that arrives at its meaning sideways. Men who sit across a table from him fifty years later, in London and in Abu Dhabi, will describe the same manner and reach for the same word, mysticism, because they have no banking word for it. He learns it here before he learns arithmetic.
suggested_refs: The Urdu-speaking service families of Lucknow after the fall of Awadh
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: University of Lucknow, the degrees in English and law
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no source gives any year for his enrolment or graduation, and the date here is counted backwards from the 1946 start of his banking career
stops.campa: He takes a master's degree in English literature and a bachelor's in law. Nobody records the years. The literature is the part that shows: the speeches he gives to his own staff for the next four decades are built like sermons, with a text, an exposition, and a turn, and they ask questions no memorandum asks. The law is the part that does not show, and that later matters more, because a man who has read law knows precisely which jurisdiction is asking the question and which one is not.
suggested_refs: The University of Lucknow arts and law faculties in the last decade of British India
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Bombay, the desk at Habib Bank
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month is a default, and no source places him in a named office of the bank
stops.campa: At twenty-four he joins Habib Bank Limited, founded in Bombay five years earlier and one of the few Muslim-owned banks in India operating at any scale. He arrives a year before the country he is working in ceases to exist. What he learns in the Bombay office is correspondent banking, the practice of holding accounts for banks in places where you have no branch, which is the whole of his later career stated in one sentence. He also learns whom the bank belongs to, and that a bank belongs to somebody.
suggested_refs: Habib Bank Limited, established Bombay 1941
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'
Wikipedia, 'Habib Bank Limited'

stops.name: Karachi, arrival in a country three months old
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the migration is attested but no source gives his route, his crossing date, or his port
stops.campa: Partition moves the border across him and he goes with it, one man in a migration of millions, into a state that has existed for weeks. Karachi is the capital and the port, taking in refugees faster than it can put roofs over them, a city of tents and ledgers. He arrives with two degrees and a year of banking. He has also been useful to an institution that is moving to Karachi in the same months he is, and the institution remembers it. Within a year he has a desk again.
suggested_refs: The refugee settlement of Karachi, 1947-1951
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: I.I. Chundrigar Road, Karachi, the bank that moved with him
stops.date_confidence: attested for the bank's relocation; Abedi's own presence in the Karachi head office is inference
stops.campa: On the seventh of August, at Jinnah's request, Habib Bank moves its head office from Bombay to Karachi, and the institution Abedi joined in one country reopens in another. He rises inside it through the 1950s on the street that will become the country's financial spine, learning the patronage side of banking as thoroughly as the ledger side: which families are owed, which are owing, which minister takes a call. The colleagues he gathers in this decade will follow him out of the building in 1959.
suggested_refs: Habib Bank Plaza and the banking street of I.I. Chundrigar Road
sources: Wikipedia, 'Habib Bank Limited'
Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: I.I. Chundrigar Road, the founding of United Bank
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested for the first branch opening
stops.campa: In November he opens United Bank Limited on the same street, taking a cohort of Habib Bank men with him and becoming its first president at thirty-seven. The method that will build and destroy everything after is already formed here: expand faster than the competition can price, recruit by personal loyalty rather than by pedigree, and take the depositors nobody respectable wants. Within a decade UBL is the second-largest bank in Pakistan, built by men who owe him their careers.
suggested_refs: United Bank Limited, first branch, I.I. Chundrigar Road, November 1959
sources: Wikipedia, 'United Bank Limited'
Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Abu Dhabi, the court of Sheikh Zayed
stops.date_confidence: the accession date is attested; the pool's 1965 dating is corrected, since Zayed was not ruler of Abu Dhabi before this day
stops.campa: On the sixth of August, Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan replaces his brother Shakhbut as ruler of Abu Dhabi, thirty-eight years of one reign ending without a shot. Abedi becomes his banker and then something with no title, the man who handles what a treasury would handle if the emirate had built one yet. Petrodollars are arriving in a quantity that is remaking the Gulf and, through it, London. In Tehran the Shah is riding the same flood; Abedi's arrangement is that he does not need to own the oil, only the account it settles into.
suggested_refs: The accession of Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, 6 August 1966
sources: Wikipedia, 'Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan'
Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Karachi, the second bank of Pakistan
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the rank is attested but no source dates the moment UBL reached it
stops.campa: UBL passes into second place among Pakistan's banks, and Abedi has what he needs: a balance sheet large enough to be introduced by, and a country small enough to have outgrown. He is flying to the Gulf, where the oil states are beginning to receive more money each quarter than their institutions know how to hold, and where the Pakistani labourers building those states send their wages home through whoever will carry them. He is the one who offers to carry them.
suggested_refs: Pakistani labour remittance flows into the Trucial States, 1960s
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Luxembourg City, the incorporation
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted
stops.campa: He registers the Bank of Credit and Commerce International in Luxembourg with about two and a half million dollars, Sheikh Zayed holding seventy-five percent and the Bank of America twenty-five, which comes in on his condition that the management style stays his. Luxembourg is chosen for what it does not do: it licenses readily, supervises lightly, and has no appetite for asking where a deposit was standing yesterday. The choice is not a convenience of the founding. It is the founding.
stops.quote: Bank of America agreed to become a shareholder, but we made it a condition that we would establish the management style.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Agha Hasan Abedi, cited in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3; seen only via summarized fetch, not verified verbatim
suggested_refs: The Luxembourg banking register, BCCI SA, 1972
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'
US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3

stops.name: Leadenhall Street, London, the head office that is not the seat
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the London operating base; the month is a default and the specific street is carried without independent citation
stops.campa: The operations open in the City the same year the charter is signed in Luxembourg, so that from its first month the bank has a head office in one country and a legal seat in another, and no regulator anywhere sees the whole animal. London supplies the correspondent relationships and the presumption of respectability that a City postcode confers on anyone holding it. Mosaddegh's London, the London of oil arrangements made in offices and unmade elsewhere, absorbs it without comment.
suggested_refs: BCCI's City of London operational headquarters, from 1972
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: George Town, Grand Cayman, BCCI Overseas
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Cayman entity is attested but no source reached dates its registration
stops.campa: A third jurisdiction is added. The group divides into BCCI Holdings, with BCCI SA in Luxembourg beneath it and BCCI Overseas in Grand Cayman beside that, and the two halves are audited by different firms: Price Waterhouse takes the Cayman books, Ernst and Young the London and Luxembourg ones, and the mandates are not consolidated into a single auditor until 1987. Meyer Lansky had built the same shape out of Swiss numbers and Nassau by 1959, for a criminal network. Abedi builds it for a sovereign one.
suggested_refs: BCCI Overseas Ltd, Grand Cayman, and the split audit mandate
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Geneva, the purchase of Banque de Commerce et Placements
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted
stops.campa: He buys a respectable old Swiss house and folds it in, adding banking secrecy law to a structure already built on jurisdictional fog. The same year the network passes from nineteen branches in five countries to a hundred and eight branches, and assets go from about two hundred million dollars to one and a six-tenths billion. Nobody in banking has grown at this rate. The trade press begins calling it the fastest-growing bank in the world, and keeps calling it that for ten years.
suggested_refs: Banque de Commerce et Placements, Geneva, acquired 1976
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, the earliest arrival
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the source says early 1980s and gives no year
stops.campa: BCCI opens inside China's new Special Economic Zone at Shenzhen, among the first foreign banks through the door of Deng Xiaoping's opening, at a moment when the zone is still mostly fields and the Western banks are still writing memoranda about risk. The rule is the same in every market he enters: arrive before the ground is surveyed, and hold the position while the competition is still deciding whether the country is real. He enters Africa on the same principle in 1979.
suggested_refs: Foreign bank entry into the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, early 1980s
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Fleet Street, London, a touch of mysticism in banking
stops.date_confidence: the interview's publication date is attested by footnote in the Senate report; the Fleet Street pin stands for the newspaper, not for a recorded meeting place
stops.campa: A British journalist interviews him and files a piece headlined as the man who adds a touch of mysticism to banking. Abedi gives him the sentence that the Senate of the United States will still be quoting fourteen years later, and it is not evasion; it is an accurate description of the business model, delivered in public to a newspaper, and understood by nobody who reads it as anything but eastern colour. He tells them what the bank is for and they print it as charm.
stops.quote: Western Banks concentrate on the visible, whereas we stress the invisible.
stops.quote_source: Agha Hasan Abedi, Financial Times, 17 May 1978, reprinted at S. Hrg. 102-350 Pt. 3 p. 303, cited in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3, n. 47
suggested_refs: Financial Times, 'The man who adds a touch of mysticism to banking', 17 May 1978
sources: US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3

stops.name: Threadneedle Street, the licence refused
stops.date_confidence: the interview is dated July 1978 by footnote; the Bank of England pin stands for the institution refusing, not for a meeting
stops.campa: The Bank of England declines to give BCCI a full banking licence, and the bank operates in the City for the next thirteen years without one, supervised by nobody in particular. Abedi answers in the press with a grievance rather than an application, and names the thing he believes is refusing him. He is describing an establishment, and he is not wrong that one exists. He is wrong about what it would take to join it, and he will spend a decade buying at retail what it never sells.
stops.quote: The Bank of England probably hasn't given permission because of the atmosphere surrounding the BCCI and the propaganda that has been spread about us. . . It is not only the Bank of England that is against us, but the Club.
stops.quote_source: Agha Hasan Abedi, Euromoney, July 1978, S. Hrg. 102-350 Pt. 3 p. 308, cited in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3, n. 70
suggested_refs: The Bank of England's supervision of BCCI, 1978-1991
sources: US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3
Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Washington, First American Bankshares behind Clark Clifford
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the purchase and for the start of Clifford's chairmanship; month defaulted
stops.campa: Clients of BCCI buy Financial General Bankshares and rename it First American. Clark Clifford, adviser to presidents since Truman, takes the chair, and his presence is the whole instrument: American law forbids a foreign bank to control a domestic one undisclosed, and no regulator interrogates a bank chaired by that man. BCCI holds roughly sixty percent or more through Arab nominees and pledged stock. It stands for nine years, until a Price Waterhouse audit in 1990 reads the pledges.
stops.quote: I found him to be pleasant and a man of importance.
stops.quote_source: Clark Clifford on first meeting Agha Hasan Abedi, December 1977, per US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 13; seen via summarized fetch only
suggested_refs: First American Bankshares, Washington, chaired by Clark Clifford 1982-1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'
Wikipedia, 'Clark Clifford'
US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 13

stops.name: Sloane Street, Knightsbridge, the special duties accounts
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the branch and its Abu Nidal accounts are attested, but no source dates them to a year
stops.campa: The Knightsbridge branch holds accounts later traced to the Abu Nidal Organization, run through a private client desk and a department the bank calls special duties. Retail customers queue at the same counter. Investigators reconstructing it afterwards find intelligence services, arms dealers, and Libyan state money in the same ledgers Gaddafi's officers could have walked to from Hyde Park. Whether Abedi vetted any single account is disputed and undocumented. That the institution would hold them is not.
suggested_refs: BCCI's private client and 'special duties' departments, Sloane Street
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Panama City, the general's account
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the Noriega accounts are attested, the branch-level mechanism and the year are not
stops.campa: Manuel Noriega banks with BCCI. He has been on an American intelligence payroll since he was a cadet, thirty-one years of payments by the later count of federal prosecutors, and he runs a country that is also a canal and also a bank. The two arrangements fit each other exactly: a man who cannot be paid openly, and an institution whose entire proposition is that a deposit need not say where it slept last night. Four years on, an American invasion will take him out of it.
suggested_refs: BCCI's Panama operations and the Noriega accounts
sources: working/journeys/QUEUE.md
working/journeys/manuel_noriega.journey.json
Britannica, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Leadenhall Street, London, the annual address to the managers
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the address is quoted in the Senate report without a date, and the 1985 placement follows a separately dated address to forty-five managers that year
stops.campa: He stands in front of his own managers and asks them a question that has no answer in banking. His staff call the bank a family, then a God-gifted entity connected to the universe, and the phrases are his; the Senate investigators who later read these transcripts file them under mysticism, and note that the same speeches also instructed men to bring in deposits by whatever route the deposits came. Both readings are supported by the text. The bank is run on the register of a religious order and audited like a shipping line.
stops.quote: IS BCC A DESIRE, OR IS BCC A BANK?
stops.quote_source: Agha Hasan Abedi, internal BCCI management address, quoted in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3, n. 62
suggested_refs: BCCI internal management conference transcripts, cited in The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3
sources: US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3

segments.name: Infaq: the Money Turned Back Toward Pakistan

stops.name: Islamabad, sector G-9, the FAST institute
stops.date_confidence: year and endowment attested; the pool's Karachi siting is corrected to Islamabad, and the pin is sector-level rather than a surveyed address
stops.campa: He endows the BCCI Foundation for Advancement of Science and Technology with a hundred million rupees and it opens as the FAST Institute of Computer Science, headquartered in sector G-9. Pakistan in 1980 has almost no computing faculty. The institution outlives the bank by dropping its initials: it becomes the National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, formally inaugurated in July 2000, and now runs six campuses. Its founder's name is not on the gate.
suggested_refs: The FAST Institute of Computer Science, Islamabad, endowed 1980
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'
Wikipedia, 'National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences'

stops.name: Karachi, the single office of the Infaq Foundation
stops.date_confidence: the 1983 start of Ghulam Ishaq Khan's chairmanship is attested and stands for the foundation's operating date; month defaulted
stops.campa: The Infaq Foundation runs out of one Karachi office and holds capital and reserves above two and a half billion rupees, funded from the profits of a bank in Luxembourg. Its beneficiaries are hospitals and engineering schools: the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation, the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Lady Dufferin Hospital, which was taking in patients before his grandfather was born. Ghulam Ishaq Khan chairs it from 1983 to 1995, the last seven of those years as President of Pakistan.
suggested_refs: The Infaq Foundation, Karachi, and its listed beneficiary institutions
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Karachi, the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Wikipedia's Abedi article lists SIUT among Infaq beneficiaries, while SIUT's own article credits Adeebul Hasan Rizvi and never mentions Infaq, and no source dates the funding
stops.campa: SIUT stands next to the Civil Hospital and treats kidney patients free of charge, which in Pakistan in the 1980s is not a policy but an argument. One source lists it among the Infaq Foundation's beneficiaries. Its own history names a different founder, Adeebul Hasan Rizvi, dates itself to a hospital department opened in 1970, and does not mention Abedi's foundation anywhere. The contradiction is not resolved here. The institute is still open, and does not print either version on its wall.
suggested_refs: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation, Karachi, autonomous from 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'
Wikipedia, 'Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation'

stops.name: Islamabad, the president who chairs the foundation
stops.date_confidence: the date of Ghulam Ishaq Khan's assumption of the presidency; no meeting between him and Abedi is documented in any source reached
stops.campa: Zia dies in the air over Bahawalpur and Ghulam Ishaq Khan takes the presidency, having chaired Abedi's foundation for five years and continuing to chair it for seven more. Inside Pakistan the bank is a national champion and a patron of universities. Outside it, regulators in four capitals are assembling a case that will end with the phrase fraud of the century. Both descriptions are current in the same year, and the men who hold one of them do not mention the other.
suggested_refs: Ghulam Ishaq Khan, chairman of the Infaq Foundation 1983-1995 and President of Pakistan from 1988
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Topi, Swabi, the Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute
stops.date_confidence: founding year and donation figures attested; month defaulted, and the coordinates follow Wikipedia against a rival figure in the research pool thirty kilometres west
stops.campa: Above the Indus at Topi, the Infaq Foundation puts seven hundred and fifty million rupees into an engineering institute named for its own chairman, on top of fifty million given in December 1985. It becomes one of the most selective schools in the country. Its auditorium seats five hundred and thirty-five and is named the Agha Hasan Abedi Auditorium, so that his name survives in public as a room in the hills where nineteen-year-olds sit their exams under it.
suggested_refs: The Agha Hasan Abedi Auditorium, GIK Institute, Topi
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology'
Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Tampa, the opening of Operation C-Chase
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted
stops.campa: United States Customs sends Special Agent Robert Mazur into BCCI's Tampa division carrying a false name and an account to open. What he finds is not a bank being used by launderers but a bank soliciting them, offering the service as a service, priced. The Colombian cartel money moves through Florida accounts for two years while the agent takes notes. Everything American investigators later know about the institution begins in a branch office in Florida, and none of it begins in London.
suggested_refs: US Customs Operation C-Chase, Tampa, 1986-1988
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Tampa, the wedding that was not one
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the sting's conclusion; the month is reconstruction, the source giving only the year and the device
stops.campa: The two-year operation ends with a fake wedding, the invitations going out to the bankers who have been laundering for the agent, the arrests made as the guests arrive. BCCI officers are indicted. The bank's public face holds for a while longer on the argument that Tampa was a rogue office. That argument requires the head office not to have known, and the head office is in London, which no American prosecutor can reach and no British regulator has licensed.
suggested_refs: The C-Chase wedding sting and the 1988 indictments of BCCI officers
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: London, the heart transplant
stops.date_confidence: the transplant year is attested; the location is NOT attested, no source names a city or hospital, and this London pin is conjecture drawn from his UK medical treatment, carried here flagged rather than as a finding
stops.campa: He receives a new heart and leaves the running of BCCI, sixteen years after signing the Luxembourg charter. No source reached names the hospital or the city; the pin here is an inference from where he was treated and should be read as one. His chief financial officer, asked three years later what the man had been like, does not answer with a fact about banking, and the sentence he offers instead is the one the Senate prints. The bank continues without him, which is the discovery of the next two years: it can.
stops.quote: I remember looking into his eyes and seeing God and the Devil balanced equally in them.
stops.quote_source: Massihur Rahman, BCCI chief financial officer, staff interview 7 August 1991, quoted in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3
suggested_refs: Abedi's 1988 heart transplant, location unrecorded in accessible sources
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'
US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3

stops.name: Tampa, the plea on the ground of respondeat superior
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted
stops.campa: After a six-month trial and under heavy pressure from American authorities, BCCI pleads guilty to money laundering, but only on the doctrine that a company answers for the acts of its servants. It pays ten million dollars in fines and forfeits five hundred and fifty million in American assets, and admits nothing about anybody's intent. It is a plea designed to leave a bank standing, and it works: no officer of the London head office is touched by it, and no regulator outside the United States treats it as a finding about the group. It buys eighteen more months.
suggested_refs: The 1990 BCCI guilty plea, fine and forfeiture
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Abu Dhabi, seventy-eight percent
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the audit, the loss, and the shareholding; month defaulted
stops.campa: A Price Waterhouse audit finds losses in the hundreds of millions, and the bank goes back to the man it started with. Zayed makes the loss good and takes his stake to seventy-eight percent, buying a year and a half of continued existence. The relationship that opened in 1966 with a ruler's private accounts closes as a rescue of a global institution by one family's treasury. The same audit is reading the First American pledges in Washington at the same time, and that discovery does not stay bought.
suggested_refs: The 1990 Price Waterhouse audit and the Abu Dhabi recapitalisation
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Karachi, the heart attack and the severance
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month is a default, and Wikipedia gives only 'Pakistan' as the place
stops.campa: A heart attack, two years after the transplant, and he formally cuts his connection with BCCI. He is sixty-eight and in Pakistan, and from this point he never leaves it. Colleagues interviewed afterwards describe a man who wept when confronted, who could not be argued with, and whose grip on the institution had been personal to the last and was now gone. The bank has eight months left and no longer has the only person who understood how it was assembled.
stops.quote: I said, Mr. Abedi you are making things very difficult ... He started crying.
stops.quote_source: Abdur Sakhia, BCCI officer, staff interview 7 October 1991, quoted in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 3; ellipsis in the cited text
suggested_refs: Abedi's 1990 severance from BCCI
sources: Wikipedia, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'
US Senate, The BCCI Affair (1992), Ch. 3

stops.name: London, Price Waterhouse asked to look properly
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested
stops.campa: In March the Bank of England, which never licensed BCCI and never stopped it either, commissions Price Waterhouse to inquire into its affairs. The firm has audited half the group for years. It is now being asked to describe, to a regulator, what the arrangement it half-audited actually was. Three months of work follow, under a codename, and the report that comes out of it is not circulated to depositors, to staff, or to anybody in the seventy-odd countries where the bank is still open for business tomorrow morning.
suggested_refs: The Bank of England's March 1991 instruction to Price Waterhouse
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: London, the Sandstorm report
stops.date_confidence: full date attested
stops.campa: On the twenty-fourth of June the report reaches the Bank of England under the codename Sandstorm and describes fraud and manipulation running through the institution rather than through any one branch of it. The losses are put between ten and seventeen billion dollars. Eleven days pass. In those eleven days the branches open, the tellers count, and roughly a million depositors in dozens of countries put money into an institution the regulators of two continents have already agreed is finished.
suggested_refs: The Sandstorm report, submitted 24 June 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Threadneedle Street, one o'clock in the afternoon
stops.date_confidence: full date attested; the entry time of 1pm London and 8am New York is attested
stops.campa: At one in the afternoon London time, eight in the morning in New York, regulators walk into BCCI offices in seven countries at once. It is the largest coordinated banking seizure ever attempted and it is done at speed because the alternative is a run. Thirteen years after refusing the bank a licence, the Bank of England ends it in an afternoon, having supervised it in the interval no more closely than it licensed it. Depositors across three continents learn what has happened from a locked door and a printed notice, and nobody has told them anything for the eleven days since the report landed.
suggested_refs: The coordinated regulatory closure of BCCI, 5 July 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Luxembourg City, the liquidation order
stops.date_confidence: full date attested
stops.campa: The court in the jurisdiction that chartered the bank in 1972 orders it wound up on the same day the offices are entered. Nineteen years, from a registration in a small European capital to a liquidation in the same building, and the intervening structure is so distributed that liquidators will spend a decade establishing who owed what to whom. Around a million depositors are affected immediately. Most of them are in countries that never had a vote in how the bank was supervised.
suggested_refs: The Luxembourg liquidation order of 5 July 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'
Britannica, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Hong Kong, two days behind London
stops.date_confidence: full date attested for the closure order; formal liquidation on 17 July is attested
stops.campa: The Commissioner of Banking closes the local branches on the seventh, two days after London, and formal liquidation follows on the seventeenth. The gap of two days is not deliberation; it is the speed at which a fear of a run travels around the world in 1991. Depositors in the territory lose access without notice. Regulators are still reconstructing what the branches actually held years afterwards, because the ledgers that would say are in three other jurisdictions.
suggested_refs: The Hong Kong closure and liquidation of BCCI branches, July 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Manhattan, the indictment of a man who will not come
stops.date_confidence: full date attested for the indictment; the attribution to District Attorney Robert Morgenthau personally is widely reported but not sourced in this pass
stops.campa: A grand jury returns twelve counts against Abedi and against Swaleh Naqvi, the chief executive who ran the bank after the transplant. The charges include fraud, bribery, and money laundering. The defendant is in Karachi with a transplanted heart, and Pakistan will not send him. From this day forward the largest banking fraud yet recorded has a named architect who is formally accused, permanently reachable by post, and never once inside a courtroom.
suggested_refs: The New York indictment of Abedi and Naqvi, 29 July 1991
sources: Wikipedia, 'Bank of Credit and Commerce International'

stops.name: Capitol Hill, the Kerry Committee reports
stops.date_confidence: month and year of publication attested; the hearings ran across 1991 and 1992
stops.campa: Senator John Kerry's subcommittee publishes its report on BCCI's ties to intelligence services, arms dealing, and Manuel Noriega, and its findings implicate American regulators and agencies as thoroughly as they implicate the bank. Abedi does not testify; he is incapacitated in Karachi after the 1988 transplant and the 1990 heart attack, and no source records an attempt to compel him. The committee's witnesses describe him instead, and their descriptions do not agree with each other.
stops.quote: Every instance o[r] report that I either got or from what Mr. Clifford told me came back that Mr. Abedi was a man of integrity and character.
stops.quote_source: Bert Lance, testimony, S. Hrg. 102-350 Pt. 3 p. 6, quoted in US Senate, The BCCI Affair, Ch. 13, n. 6

stops.campa: Lord Justice Bingham reports to the British government on how the Bank of England supervised BCCI for the length of its life and did not stop it. The document embarrasses the regulator as much as it condemns the bank, and its subject is not Abedi; it is the question of what a supervisor is for. He is named throughout as the architect nobody in London investigated while he was standing in London and could have been asked. He is in Karachi, and will not be asked now.

segments.name: The Defendant Who Cannot Be Fetched

stops.name: Abu Dhabi, convicted where the money came from
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; Britannica gives no date for the UAE conviction, the research pool offered 1994 and 1994-1995, and whether the trial was formally in absentia is not stated in any source reached
stops.campa: A court in the United Arab Emirates convicts him and sentences him to eight years. He is in Karachi and does not attend. The emirate whose ruler funded the bank in 1972, took it to seventy-eight percent in 1990, and lost most of what he put in, is the only jurisdiction on earth that convicts the founder of anything at all. The sentence is never served, never appealed, and never tested against a body, and the man it names outlives it by a year in a city two thousand kilometres away, where nobody is asking for him.
suggested_refs: The UAE prosecutions arising from the BCCI collapse
sources: Britannica, 'Agha Hasan Abedi'

stops.name: Karachi, the extradition that is refused
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the refusal is reported without a date, and the month and day are defaults
stops.campa: He remains under indictment in the United States and the United Kingdom, and Pakistan declines to hand him over, calling the prosecutions politically motivated. The state that has not yet decorated him also does not surrender him. He lives out his last years in the city he arrived at in 1947 with two degrees and a year of banking, in a country where the foundation he endowed is chaired by the man who was until recently its president, and where no court has ever asked him a question.

stops.name: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi, the death
stops.date_confidence: full date attested; the cause is given as heart failure in one passage of the cited article and heart attack in another, and the contradiction is left standing
stops.campa: He dies on the fifth of August at the Aga Khan University Hospital, seventy-three years old, four years and a month after the doors were locked in seven countries on one afternoon. The heart that was replaced in 1988 stops. He dies a convicted man in one jurisdiction, an accused man in two more, and a benefactor in the one he is lying in, and no proceeding anywhere has established a single fact about him under oath. The hospital is eleven years old, built with Aga Khan money and government land, and owes his foundation nothing.

stops.name: Karachi, the grave nobody names
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no source reached names the cemetery, the grave, or any marker, a Find a Grave lookup returned HTTP 403, and this pin is the city, not a burial site
stops.campa: He is buried in Karachi and no accessible source says where. The obituaries carry the death, the age, and the cause, and stop at the hospital door. The man who put his name on an auditorium in the hills of Swabi, and took it off a university in Islamabad, has no located grave in anything reachable, and no shrine, no anniversary, no folk story attached to him in the sources checked. This is recorded as a gap in the record and not as a finding about the record.

stops.name: Arlington National Cemetery, the chairman is buried
stops.date_confidence: full date of death attested; the Arlington interment is attested
stops.campa: Clark Clifford dies at ninety-one and is buried at Arlington, adviser to four presidents and chairman of the bank BCCI owned without saying so. He was indicted in 1992; the charges were dropped in 1993 on grounds of his health; in 1998 he and Robert Altman settled with the Federal Reserve for five million dollars. He was never convicted, and the affair is in the first paragraph of every account of him. He described what was left to him as a choice between two verdicts.
stops.quote: I have a choice of either seeming stupid or venal.
stops.quote_source: Clark Clifford to the New York Times, on the First American affair; reported without a dated citation in the research pool

stops.name: Islamabad, the Hilal-i-Imtiaz
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted, and the award is the second grade of the Order of Imtiaz, not the first, correcting the research pool
stops.campa: Twenty years after his death and twenty-four after the seizure, the Pakistani state awards him the Hilal-i-Imtiaz, the second grade in the Order of Imtiaz. Abroad his name attaches to the largest banking fraud of the century. At home it attaches to a university, an engineering institute, a foundation, and now a decoration. Nothing is retracted on either side. Two records of the same man run in parallel in two hemispheres, and neither is required to answer the other.

stops.name: Washington, the Comptroller says the name again
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested
stops.campa: In March the acting Comptroller of the Currency, Michael J. Hsu, tells an audience that there are strong parallels between FTX and the Bank of Credit and Commerce International. Thirty-two years after the doors were locked, an American regulator reaches for the same three letters to explain a new institution nobody could see into. Its founder said in a newspaper in 1978 that the bank stressed the invisible. The sentence has outlasted the bank by thirty-two years.
